thesis: Ancient and early modern cases recover authentic religious contexts while resisting anachronism and unsupported discovery legends.

ideas.statement: Thales, Pythagoras, Descartes, Pascal and Leibniz illustrate that inspiration, symbolism and existential argument do not determine mathematical or metaphysical validity.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Later testimony limits ancient attribution; Pascal’s wager concerns decision under uncertainty, not proof; binary representation works independently of its theological symbolism.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Later testimony limits ancient attribution; Pascal’s wager concerns decision under uncertainty, not proof; binary representation works independently of its theological symbolism.

audit.notes: All source units read directly; qualifications retained and navigation excluded.
